source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 10, Schedule 1 Line 48b; PDF page 24, Pension and Annuity Worksheet Line 1 (MFJ, under 100,000: do not complete, subtract Line 5b); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 50,000.00 + private pension 40,000.00 = 90,000.00. Federal taxable income = 90,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 58,500.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 90,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 90,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 48b pension and annuity (Line 5b part): federal AGI 90,000.00 is under the 100,000.00 test, decimal 1; 40,000.00 x 1 = 40,000.00 -> 40,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 40,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 40,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 90,000.00 - 40,000.00 = 50,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 50,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 50,000.00 is more than 49,000.00, exemption 22,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 50,000.00 - 22,000.00 = 28,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 28,000.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 8,000.00 x 0.045 = 400.00 + 360.00 = 760.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 50,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 760.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.15 (Connecticut AGI 50,000.00 is in the band more than 41,500.00); Line 9 = 760.00 x 0.15 = 114.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 760.00 - 114.00 = 646.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: No age test: the 58-year-old's private pension is subtracted in full because federal AGI is under 100,000.
